title: Two Sum in one pass with a HashMap

blocks.text: The page's Q4 turns the brute-force O(n^2) "check every pair" into O(n): walk the array once, and for each element look up its *complement* (`target - nums[i]`) in a HashMap of the values seen so far, mapped to their indices.
Write `TwoSum.find(nums, target)`: return `{i, j}` with `i < j` and `nums[i] + nums[j] == target`. Each test input has at most one such pair.

items: **An element never pairs with itself**: index `i` is used once.
**Two equal values at different indices can pair.**
**No pair gives an empty array** (`new int[0]`), never `null`.

cases.says: In [2, 7, 11, 15] the pair for 9 is [0, 1]; in [-3, 4, 3, 90] the pair for 0 is [0, 2].
In [3, 2, 4] the pair for 6 is [1, 2], not the 3 at index 0 used twice.
In [3, 3] the pair for 6 is [0, 1]: two different elements with the same value.
When no two elements add up to the target the answer is an empty array, not null.

concepts: A HashMap of values seen so far turns the O(n^2) pair search of Two Sum into one O(n) pass at the cost of O(n) space.
